title: Cross-Repo Architecture and Security Review Gate
public_repo_rule: This report contains only public-safe metadata, commit ids, test outcomes and review findings; it stores no secrets, raw prompts, raw responses, document text or provider credentials.

reviewed_repos.name: inkognitroz.github.io
reviewed_repos.role: Static MMIR.ai app shell, chat UI, progress dashboard, no-secret public evidence and GitHub Pages deployment.

reviewed_repos.name: mimir-backend-template
reviewed_repos.role: Protected managed API template for owner-scoped data, provider routing, auth, remediation gates and audit-safe backend workflows.

evidence.result: All smoke checks passed locally after D251.
evidence.scope: Visible controls, first-chat activation, model/no-model states, remediation timeline, public dashboard and route evidence.
Blocks secret-like strings, real-looking key assignment, browser bearer construction and enabled paid/provider key flows in public assets.
Public copy stays MMIR.ai aligned and avoids stale Mimir/MMIR drift.

evidence.result: MMIR API route manifest check passed for 74 public route entries.
evidence.scope: Frontend route expectations remain explicit and public-safe.
Auth, RBAC, memory, knowledge, model registry, node registry, sharing, corrections, remediation, routing, billing gates, training plans and workflow stores.

evidence.result: Managed API route manifest check passed for 125 backend route entries.
evidence.scope: Protected API surface is documented and contract-checked.
Private backend template remains free of committed provider keys and tokens.

evidence.result: Static quality gates, public branding migration and GitHub Pages deploy succeeded for commit 96de2fb.
evidence.scope: Remote CI agrees with local quality gates for the latest public deployment.

architecture_scorecard.finding: The public GitHub Pages repo acts as a non-authoritative UI and evidence surface; protected mutation, provider keys and owner-scoped storage stay behind the private backend template.
architecture_scorecard.next_action: Keep public-safety audit in both deploy and quality workflows.

architecture_scorecard.finding: Correction remediation, execution, rollback and autopilot flows stop before sensitive source mutation unless an explicit protected backend route confirms the action.
architecture_scorecard.next_action: Continue adding backend-only gates before any new source mutation or paid route.

architecture_scorecard.finding: Current public and backend tests keep paid routes disabled unless explicitly approved; free/local/mock routes are the default path.
architecture_scorecard.next_action: Make every new user journey show a free first action before paid/provider options.

architecture_scorecard.finding: Public and backend route manifests both pass independently, but the platform does not yet publish one merged cross-repo drift report.
architecture_scorecard.next_action: Fold route drift into the next activation canary or a dedicated route parity check.

architecture_scorecard.finding: Deterministic fixtures cover desktop/mobile selectors and no-overlap contracts, but live in-app browser automation was unstable in this thread.
architecture_scorecard.next_action: Prefer fixture gates now; restore live browser screenshot checks when the browser bridge is stable.

code_review_findings.finding: No high-severity secret leakage or public authority regression was found in the latest public changes.
code_review_findings.next_action: Keep public repo public-safe; do not place backend secrets, provider keys or paid route credentials in GitHub Pages.

code_review_findings.finding: Backend remediation gates enforce explicit confirmation, owner scope and rollback metadata before supported source changes.
code_review_findings.next_action: Continue using backend-only execution and rollback routes for source mutation.

code_review_findings.finding: Many beta UI controls now have individual smoke coverage, but the highest user-fit risk is still the end-to-end free activation path feeling fragmented across first screen, model selection, local node and chat receipt.
code_review_findings.next_action: D253 should add one no-spend end-to-end activation canary from first visit to first useful answer receipt.

code_review_findings.finding: Live browser screenshot QA could not be trusted in this thread because the in-app browser bridge timed out; deterministic fixture QA is green but not a full visual replacement.
code_review_findings.next_action: Keep fixture QA mandatory and reintroduce live screenshot checks once the browser bridge is reliable.

security_review.zero_trust_summary: Public UI stays non-authoritative, session/provider secrets are not stored in public localStorage, paid routes are blocked by policy unless explicitly approved and backend routes enforce owner scope.
must_not_do: Do not make inkognitroz.github.io private while it is the GitHub Pages source unless deployment is moved.
Do not store provider API keys, cloud credentials or pairing tokens in public assets.
Do not let public JavaScript execute source mutation, rollback, paid provider or tunnel routes without protected backend confirmation.

ux_review.best_current_path: Free-first activation with MMIR Guide/browser helper fallback, guided local connector repair, model library handoff, first chat receipt and Progress Dashboard evidence.
ux_review.main_gap: The parts are present, but the user still needs one coherent canary that proves a new visitor can get a useful first answer without manual configuration or paid services.

next.label: end-to-end free activation canary
next.why: The review gate shows the next highest user-fit risk is proving the whole no-spend first-use journey as one simple, useful flow.
